### Summary

When a run is split over several processes, a few decisions must come out the same on every one of them: the
length of the next time step, whether to redo a step, and whether to stop on a signal. If two processes disagreed,
their blocks would no longer advance together. This section lists the global reductions that make those decisions,
what each one combines, and which of them give the same result on any number of processes.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Makes the decisions every rank must share (time step, redo, stop) identical on every process.

**Data.** Small host tensors: the local stable step, seven redo flags, the signal count, the global-phase sums.

**Placement.** Once per step in `MeshImpl` (`max_time_step`, `check_redo`), in the global phase, and at output and finalisation.

**Activation.** Always with more than one process; no option. One process reduces nothing.

**Guarantee / limits.** MIN and MAX are exact and order free; the global-phase SUM is order dependent, bounded below.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch14-collectives-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $n_{\mathrm{redo}}$ the redo count of the current step [count];
$N$ the number of terms of a sum [count] and $b_k$ its terms; $C$[^rg-9793b59d7bc0] the Courant number, `cfl`[^rg-fe505223b66c] [-], $\Theta$[^rg-abef336e38dd] the
limiter's donor factor [-] and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$[^rg-6f5d38ae36e6] the machine epsilon, all three defined in @sec-appa.

| decision | reduction | tensor | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| time step | MIN of the local stable step | 1 double | `MeshBlockImpl::global_time_step` |
| redo | MAX of 7 cause flags | 7 doubles (0 or 1) | `MeshBlockImpl::decide_retry` |
| stop on a signal | MAX of the caught-signal count | 1 int32 | `SignalHandler::CheckSignalFlags` |
| global phase (axial closure) | SUM of the blocks' partial sums | small doubles | `global_phase_sum`; see below |
| cycle line: totals, energies and meters | SUM, MIN of $\Theta$, MAX of the VIC[^rg-0726addd7156] residual, to the root | small doubles | `print_cycle_line` |
| budget output | SUM of totals, changes, boundary flows and counters; MIN of the minima | small doubles | `reduce_budget` |
| zonal means of a diagnostic output | SUM to the root | one profile per variable | `OutputType::loadDiagOutputData` |

: The collectives of one run. {#tbl-ch14-collectives}

Barriers sit at initialisation, around every combined output (@sec-ch14-netcdf, @sec-ch14-restart) and at
finalisation.

### Derivation

Why every rank takes the same decision, in four steps:

1. *A MIN or MAX returns one of its inputs.* The minimum of doubles is computed by comparisons only, with no
   arithmetic, so it is exact and equal to one of the values reduced.
2. *That input does not depend on the order.* The minimum of a finite set is the same set element whatever order the
   backend combines the values in. So every rank receives the same bits whatever the process count or backend.
3. *The decisions use MIN or MAX only.* The time step is a MIN (`global_time_step`), the redo causes and the
   signal count are MAX (`decide_retry`, `CheckSignalFlags`). So every rank takes the same step, the same redo
   decision and the same stop.
4. *A SUM is different.* A floating-point sum of $N$ terms $b_k$, combined in any order or tree, differs from the exact
   sum by at most $(N-1)\,\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_k\lvert b_k\rvert$: each of its $N-1$ additions rounds a
   partial sum bounded by $\sum_k\lvert b_k\rvert$ with relative error at most $\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}=2^{-53}$,
   as in the round-off bound of @sec-ch07-framework. Two orders can differ by twice that. The global-phase SUM of the
   axial closure is the one SUM that feeds the state (@sec-ch14-repro).

`[C14]` of `derivation_check.py` confirms steps 1 and 2 over all 720 orders of six doubles, and `[C15]` the bound of
step 4 on 300 random summation trees.

### Numerical method

**Time step.** `MeshImpl::max_time_step` takes the minimum of `local_max_time_step` over the local blocks on the
host ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::max_time_step >}}); `global_time_step` all-reduces it with MIN and returns
$2^{-n_{\mathrm{redo}}}\,C\,\Delta t$, with $n_{\mathrm{redo}}$ the current redo count and $C$ the CFL[^rg-e0adecef2ed5] number
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::global_time_step >}}). The single-block path calls the same
two functions (`MeshBlockImpl::max_time_step`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::max_time_step >}}).

**Redo.** `MeshImpl::check_redo` first checks signals. Each local block then forms its redo entries as one tensor on
its device: the density or pressure floor hit, the VIC dry clamp, the two limiter marks, the saturation-adjustment
failure, the implicit solve failure, the vapour-repair failures of the step and the heat-capacity latch
(`local_redo_flag_tensor`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}). When the
local blocks share a device, `decide_retry` stacks the tensors, takes their element-wise maximum on the device and
reads it to the host once; otherwise it reads each block's tensor and ORs them. The read folds the last two entries
into the limiter flag and returns seven flags (`read_redo_flags`,
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::read_redo_flags >}}). `decide_retry` all-reduces the seven values
with MAX and packs the result into a cause bit mask
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::decide_retry >}}). Every block on every process then applies the
same decision: a hit anywhere rolls back every block (`MeshImpl::check_redo`,
{{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::check_redo >}}). The redo itself is the subject of @sec-ch09-redo.

**Signals.** SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGALRM set flags. `CheckSignalFlags` sums the local flags with the signals blocked,
all-reduces the count with MAX, and returns it; a non-zero value makes `check_redo` return $-1$ and the driver stop.
With no snapy process group it falls back to a registered external group
(`CheckSignalFlags`, {{< code src/mesh/signal_handler.cpp SignalHandler::CheckSignalFlags >}}).

**Global phase.** With the axial closure on (@sec-ch07-axial), every block forms its partial sums on its device
(`axial_closure_sums`), the Mesh adds them in block index order, $0,1,\dots$, into a zero tensor, and one
allreduce SUM on the host combines the processes (`global_phase_sum`,
{{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp global_phase_sum >}}; {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}); a single
block reduces its own partials the same way ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}}). The
order in which the allreduce adds the processes' tensors is the backend's; the code does not fix it. Every block then
applies the same reduced sums.

**Cycle line and outputs.** On every cycle that prints a line (each `ncycle_out`[^rg-9751aed7d553]-th), `print_cycle_line`
reduces the conserved totals, the kinetic and potential energies and the limiter meters with SUM, the smallest $\Theta$
with MIN and the VIC clamp residual with MAX, each a `reduce` to the root process, which prints them
({{< code src/diagnostics/budget.cpp print_cycle_line >}}). The budget output all-reduces its records with SUM and MIN
({{< code src/diagnostics/budget.cpp reduce_budget >}}), and a diagnostic output with zonal means reduces its sums to
the root ({{< code src/output/load_diag_output_data.cpp OutputType::loadDiagOutputData >}}). These are written or
printed only; nothing in the state depends on them.

**Barriers.** `initialize` holds all processes at a barrier before the first step
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize >}}); the combines of NetCDF and restart files each have
a barrier and a mirror barrier; `finish_run` ends with a barrier and, if snapy owns the group, a shutdown
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_output.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finish_run >}}; `MeshImpl::finalize`,
{{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::finalize >}}).

### Code

**A minimal input.** None: the reductions have no option. They run whenever the launch implies more than one
process (@sec-ch14-launch), and a single process skips every collective (`has_process_group` is false).

**What is refused, and why.** Nothing is refused here. A rank that never reaches a collective leaves the others
waiting in it (Limits).

**The excerpt.** Step 3 for the time step, in `MeshBlockImpl::global_time_step`:

```cpp
  if (_playout->has_process_group())
    _playout->comm->allreduce(dt_reduce, c10d::ReduceOp::MIN);
  auto dt = dt_reduce[0].item<double>();
  return pow(2., -pintg->current_redo) * pintg->options->cfl() * dt;
```

reduces a time step over two ranks with different local steps (@sec-ch14-backends).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Signals are read only in `check_redo`, once per cycle. A rank that never reaches it (a hang elsewhere) never
  handles its signal, and the others wait in the collective; the comment in
  `CheckSignalFlags` {{< code src/mesh/signal_handler.cpp SignalHandler::CheckSignalFlags >}} says so.
- Every collective is blocking and sits on the host, so each costs a device-to-host copy on GPU (@sec-ch14-gpu).
- The global-phase SUM is a floating-point sum whose grouping changes with the decomposition (cells per block,
  blocks per process, process count) and whose order across processes is left to the backend; no test measures its
  effect on a decomposed run (@sec-ch14-repro).
:::

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-9793b59d7bc0]: $C$ — Courant number (named: acoustic, advective, vertical acoustic)

[^rg-fe505223b66c]: cfl — Courant-number limit for the time step

[^rg-abef336e38dd]: $\Theta$ — the positivity limiter's donor factor in $[0,1]$: the fraction of a requested face flux the limiter allows. Capital, because $\theta$ is the colatitude

[^rg-6f5d38ae36e6]: $\epsilon_{\mathrm{m}}$ — machine epsilon of the working precision (never bare $\epsilon$, which is $\epsilon_{\mathrm{piv}}$); {{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp machine_epsilon >}}

[^rg-0726addd7156]: VIC — vertically implicit correction

[^rg-e0adecef2ed5]: CFL — Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy

[^rg-9751aed7d553]: ncycle_out — number of cycles between printed cycle lines; 0 turns the line off
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
